section.title: Working with power series
section.p: A power series first asks where it converges. Once we are safely inside that interval, a second question begins:
section.md: \text{Can we calculate with it as if it were a polynomial?}
section.p: The answer is mostly yes, but the words “safely inside” matter. Inside the radius of convergence, power series are unusually well behaved. At endpoints, every operation must be checked again.

exercise.title: When may power series be added like polynomials?

statement.p: Inside a common region of absolute convergence, power series with the same center may be added coefficient by coefficient. In your own words, why is that safe there, and why is the common interior the guaranteed region rather than a promise about endpoints?

hint.p: Absolute convergence lets you rearrange and combine tails with finite total size. Endpoints can depend on cancellation, so they are not inherited automatically.

subsection.title: Differentiating power series
subsection.p: A finite polynomial can be differentiated term by term:
A power series can also be differentiated term by term inside its radius of convergence.

The differentiated series has the same radius of convergence R. Endpoint behavior must be checked separately.

subsection.p: This theorem is one of the reasons power series are so useful. An infinite polynomial can still be differentiated like a polynomial, as long as we stay inside its radius.

exercise.title: Why can a power series be differentiated term by term inside its radius?

statement.p: Inside the radius of convergence, an infinite polynomial may be differentiated like a finite one. In your own words, why is that a theorem rather than an algebraic reflex, and why can endpoint behavior change even though the radius stays the same?

hint.p: Differentiation is a limit operation on an infinite sum, so it needs control. The interior has a geometric safety margin; an endpoint does not, so the differentiated series must be tested there again.

exercise.title: Why is term-by-term integration often gentler than differentiation?

statement.p: Integrating a power series term by term preserves the radius and can even improve endpoint behavior. In your own words, why does dividing by n+1 help the tail, and why must endpoints still be checked after integrating?

hint.p: Integration makes coefficients smaller, so convergence can only get easier in the interior. Endpoints remain numerical series of a new shape, so they are a fresh question.

subsection.title: Why power series behave better than arbitrary series
subsection.p: Term-by-term differentiation and integration are not gifts we receive for every infinite sum of functions. They are special properties of power series inside their radius of convergence.

exercise.title: Why do power series behave better than arbitrary function series?

statement.p: Term-by-term calculus is not a gift given to every infinite sum of functions. In your own words, why does staying a fixed distance inside the radius give geometric control, and why does that control fail at the endpoints?

hint.p: On a smaller closed interval around the center, the terms are dominated by a single convergent numerical series independent of x. At an endpoint that dominating geometric bound is lost.
